subject: Realtime inference queueing causing tail-latency — reserved capacity breach
messages:
From: Emily Rogers <emily.rogers@chimebank.com>
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, support@redwood.ai
Cc: Mark Lin <mark.lin@chimebank.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: Noticeable tail-latency and 5xx spike on reserved endpoints

Hi team,

We're seeing a significant jump in 95th/99th percentile latency on our reserved endpoints starting around 08:50 PDT. Concurrently, our error rate (5xx) has increased from ~0.3% to ~3.7% during peak windows. This is impacting live transactions for a subset of users.

Attached are a short trace sample and the logs showing repeated queueing across inference requests (trace_ids included). Can someone confirm if this is coming from our side or on Redwood's reserved pool?

We need triage and any temporary mitigation ASAP — happy to hop on a call.

Thanks,
Emily Rogers
SRE Lead, ChimeBank
Attachments: chimebank_traces_may7.txt (text), sample_error_snippet.log (text)

From: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 13:45:22 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Noticeable tail-latency and 5xx spike on reserved endpoints

Looping you all in. Customer (ChimeBank) reports large 95/99 pctl latency and a 10x increase in 5xx for reserved endpoints. They attached traces and logs.

Initial look (from support logs): sustained queueing on one Dedicated GPU pool serving their reserved throughput; we appear to be hitting the capacity headroom floor for that pool during their peak windows. There are signs of throttling/backpressure when token-burst patterns hit the autoscaler boundary.

Ask: Prio (can you confirm RA/ops cause and recommended immediate mitigations?). Irene — please coordinate customer comms and let me know if we should offer immediate credits or a short-term SLA exception. Marissa — FYI for renewal/exec handoff. I'll keep the timeline and notes here.

-nikhil

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 14:05:11 -0400
Subject: Re: Fwd: Noticeable tail-latency and 5xx spike on reserved endpoints

Quick technical summary:
- Root cause: one Dedicated pool (pool-id: dp-west-43) entered sustained saturation due to an atypical burst sequence from ChimeBank (long-sequence batched calls with KV cache misses). Autoscaler policy throttled requests to preserve SLOs across tenants; for reserved customers that manifests as queueing and elevated 5xx when queues backpressure the runtime.
- Immediate mitigation (minutes): 1) shift ChimeBank to a warm burst pool (burst-tier-2) that has headroom; 2) temporarily raise their reserved throughput by +25% for next 72 hours while we normalize patterns; 3) apply targeted batching reduction for their route to reduce peak token concurrency.
- Medium (hours): patch autoscaler to be aware of reserved-customer burst tolerance for dp-west-43; enable per-customer exception to bypass cross-tenant throttling.
- Long (days): increase dp-west-43 capacity or migrate ChimeBank to a dedicated subpool backed by a reserved commit.

I've attached a short capacity graph showing the saturation window (capacity_graph_q2.png). I can run the failover to burst pool now if we have permission from the customer.

-priyom
Attachments: capacity_graph_q2.png (image)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Rogers <emily.rogers@chimebank.com>
Cc: nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 14:30:47 -0400
Subject: Re: Noticeable tail-latency and 5xx spike on reserved endpoints

Hi Emily —

Thanks for flagging this and for the traces. Extremely sorry for the disruption — this is not the experience we aim to deliver. We've diagnosed a Dedicated pool saturation event and our engineering team has a mitigation plan that can be executed immediately (failover to a warm burst pool + temporary reserved throughput uplift).

Before we execute the failover, we want your approval to:
- run a controlled failover of your production route to a warm burst pool (this is zero-downtime but may change cost billing for the window)
- apply a temporary +25% throughput bump for the next 72 hours

As a gesture for the disruption, we're prepared to offer a one-time credit for the impacted billing period and prioritize capacity changes with our infra team. I'll arrange an executive call (CTO + Head of SRE) to walk through root cause and permanent fixes.

Can you confirm permission to proceed? If yes I will instruct ops to start the controlled failover immediately and Pritom will follow up on the capacity plan.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Emily

Team — final status update and ask for exec sign-off:

- Immediate actions (May 7): performed controlled failover to burst-tier-2, applied temporary +25% reserved throughput, reduced batching on customer route. Incident reduced 95/99 pctl latency to acceptable range within 18 minutes post-failover.
- Customer impact: production degradation for ~2 hours at peak; customer approved mitigation and requested SLA credit.
- Attachments/evidence: capacity graph (capacity_graph_q2.png), support traces.

Ask / Approvals required:
1) Approve a short-term commercial addendum to increase ChimeBank's reserved commit by 30% for Q3 to avoid repeat saturation while we provision additional subpool capacity (addendum draft attached: signed_addendum_chimebank.pdf once countersigned).
2) Approve issuing a one-time billing credit (~8% of May invoice) as a customer goodwill credit; finance will need an approval ticket.
3) Execs to prioritize INF-1298 (Jira) to fast-track autoscaler changes that exempt reserved customers from cross-tenant throttling.

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/7391 | Jira INF-1298: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INF-1298

I'll schedule a 30-minute briefing with CTO and Head of Product to review root cause and timeline for permanent fixes. Please reply-all with approvals or objections.

-nikhil
